checks: The fixed-index affine images have volume fraction rho^(d−1), so their uniform mixture has the stated counting density. Permutation invariance gives cell probabilities 1/d in both laws; ties are null and conditional normalization cancels.

The cell barycentrics give normalized t density (d−1)(1−t)^(d−2). The threshold condition reduces to w_j≥1/d for t<1. The normalizer is d rho^(d−1)=(d−1)rho^(d−2), exactly that of the uniform mixture of facet homotheties. This also gives density one for the point facet.

For each label the beta predecessor gives uniform U independently of T and the conditional mean V. Reconstructing both vectors with the same T gives the two target laws, preserves the minimum index and value on the almost-sure positive-facet event, and gives the required conditional mean. Integrating the density of T from ds to 1 gives the common survival function.

For interior b the mixture coefficient is db; pointwise Jensen and the critical bound give the comparison. For b≥1/d the raised coordinate cannot be below the minimum of the others. Translating k coordinates scales volume by (1−ks)^(d−1) up to 1/k; integrating gives 1/(dk). Thus the strict failure above 1/d includes b=1.

For interior b, both nonnegative Jensen gaps must vanish. Full support and continuity promote the first gap to zero for every z and i. The affine subintervals [rho r,r] cover (0,1) by interiors, so the test is affine along each vertex ray, hence on the simplex by opposite-facet induction. Both means equal the centroid, proving the converse.

At critical b, continuity and full support extend zero conditional Jensen gap to all t and w, including boundary points. Positive beta density makes each nondegenerate segment from w to a facet vertex fully supported. A supporting line at the mean proves segment affineness, and vertex-ray induction gives slice affineness. Conversely slice affineness kills the conditional gap. This includes singleton slices at t=1 and throughout d=2. Minimum is constant on each slice but nonaffine globally; when d≥3 a positive-dimensional slice rules out a strictly convex equality test.
